brief: Copper trades at record prices with record US inventories and depleted ex-US stocks, a squeeze driven mainly by tariff distortions and short-covering, not industrial demand. This fits a broader late-cycle view: commodities keep working until energy or rates break demand, so the real question is what stops the spending, not whether the Fed hikes. An overdue tariff report keeps the front-load bid alive: July pulled a record 225k MT into US warehouses, LME warrants are 51% cancelled, and 121kt is earmarked to leave London. If the levy is confirmed, the $430/t backwardation seen in mid-August could become the new normal. Underneath is a genuine regional physical squeeze tied to scarce feedstock and smelter outages. A second, multi-year leg is power infrastructure: hyperscaler capex heading toward $1.2tn by 2027 and data centres could use about 9% of US electricity by 2035, requiring copper-intensive grids, UBS's biggest bottleneck for new capacity. Goldman flags a further upside risk: mine supply falling 0.7% this year leaves the refined surplus dependent on rising scrap use, so an EU scrap restriction could erase it. Positioning stays light, GS options 3/10, futures length 4/10. China weakness, a stronger dollar, or softer Section 232 are the main risks.
